inputs.original_text: The real question is not whether the state should rank families, but whether an inheritance system deepens inequality by giving wealth an easier path across generations. People without children should not be treated as less deserving, and families come in many forms. But “family responsibility” should not become a blanket defense of tax advantages for inherited wealth. Any review should ensure equal treatment while protecting the public resources and fairness that make society work for everyone—not just those fortunate enough to inherit.
inputs.modified_text: The real issue is who benefits when wealth passes from one generation to the next. Inheritance can entrench inequality, while tax advantages for inherited wealth shift the burden away from those already privileged and weaken resources society needs to support everyone. People without children deserve equal respect, and families should not be judged by one narrow model—but appeals to “family responsibility” must not be used to shield inherited wealth from fair taxation. Any review should put equality and the public good ahead of preserving advantages for the fortunate.
